cmsFacts: CMS says remote therapeutic monitoring (RTM) captures non-physiological data, which can be self-reported, tied to a therapeutic treatment, such as musculoskeletal or respiratory data, and can monitor treatment adherence and response.
CMS says remote physiologic monitoring requires an established patient relationship, but RTM does not.
CMS says only 1 practitioner can bill remote monitoring per patient in a 30-day period, and that RTM and remote physiologic monitoring cannot be billed together.
CMS says the 2 to 15 or 16 plus day data-collection requirement does not apply to the treatment management codes 98980, 98981, 99457 and 99458.

CMS says only practitioners eligible to bill evaluation and management services can bill remote monitoring, and that auxiliary personnel can provide it under the general supervision of the billing practitioner.
metaDescription: CPT 98981 explained: the RTM add-on for each additional 20 minutes of treatment management time. Pairing with 98980, documentation and billing mistakes.

faqs.question: Can 98981 be billed on its own?
faqs.answer: No. It is an add-on and attaches only to 98980 for the same patient and month.

faqs.question: Is there a monthly limit on 98981?
faqs.answer: Monthly unit limits apply. Confirm the current count in the Physician Fee Schedule.
